sections.html:
Mount Prospect is a Cook County village about 20 miles northwest of downtown Chicago and roughly 4 miles north of O'Hare Airport. A sale here can carry transfer charges at three levels: state, county and village. The village stamp is its own step, separate from county recording, so schedule it early.

Population is 55,395 (July 2025 estimate). The typical owner-occupied home is worth $397,400, and 68.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owners usually choose between an agent, an investor who pays cash, or a sale handled alone, and the facts below apply to all three.

sections.h2: Transfer taxes on a Mount Prospect sale
sections.html:
The Cook County Clerk lists two charges: the State of Illinois at fifty cents for each $500, and Cook County at twenty-five cents for each $500. The seller is the liable party on both. The state figure matches 35 ILCS 200/31-15.

The village adds a real estate transfer tax of its own, paid by buying a stamp. The Finance Department offers an online stamp application and in-person stamps by appointment. It also has a rebate form and an affidavit of no consideration for exempt transfers such as taking a person off a deed. Call Finance for the current village rate and who pays it.

The Clerk's site also has a lookup showing the transfer fee for each municipality in the county. Put all three charges in your net sheet early.

Cook County splits each year's property tax into two bills. For tax year 2025 the due dates were April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026, and both are behind us. Other years landed on other days, so rely on the date printed on your own bill.

The title company typically splits the year's tax between buyer and seller from the latest bill, so bring that bill and your parcel number to the closing. The Treasurer's office describes homeowner, senior, senior freeze, disability and disabled veteran exemptions that a qualifying buyer may look into afterward.

The village also runs a property tax relief grant for qualifying single-family owners, a rebate on part of the village share of the county bill. Call Finance to learn whether it is open before counting on it.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Several elementary districts divide the village, and the district for your address often matters more to buyers than the village name. Confirm it before you advertise.

  • Central Mount Prospect: Mount Prospect School District 57.
  • North and somewhat east: River Trails School District 26.
  • South and somewhat west: Elk Grove Community Consolidated School District 59.
  • Small northern, north central and northwest pockets: Buffalo Grove-Wheeling CCSD 21, Arlington Heights District 25 and Prospect Heights District 23.

Township High School District 214 covers the whole village. Park services also vary by address, with the Mount Prospect, Arlington Heights, Des Plaines, Prospect Heights and River Trails park districts all serving parts of the village.

Commuters board Metra's Union Pacific Northwest Line in the village: southeast to Ogilvie Transportation Center, northwest toward Harvard and McHenry. Pace buses cover local routes. The Metra station and the closeness to O'Hare are the location points most listings lead with, and Randhurst Village is the best-known shopping address.

The climate brings muggy summers and snowy winters, which is why inspectors look hard at roofs, sump pumps and furnaces. Have those three in good order before showings.

Illinois puts the disclosure duty in 765 ILCS 77/20: the report is completed and delivered before a contract is signed. Local buyers also ask about permit history on additions, finished basements and mechanical work.

The Village Code is posted online, and Community Development is the office for permit, inspection and code questions. For a rental, ask the village what license or inspection covers your address before you list.

  • Request permit records for work done during your ownership.
  • Resolve open code notices, since an unresolved notice can complicate the closing.
  • Confirm the water, sewer and refuse account status with the village before closing.

Any past basement water belongs on the report, with repair invoices on hand.

sections.h2: Agent, owner sale or cash buyer
sections.html:
Listing through an agent reaches the most people, with showings, inspections and a lender's schedule attached. An updated house in a favored school zone may draw competing offers.

  • Agent: fits a house that shows well and an owner able to wait out a standard closing.
  • Owner sale: skips the listing fee but leaves the disclosure form, contract and stamp paperwork to you.
  • Cash buyer: fewer conditions and a closing date you may help choose, at an offer reduced for needed repairs.

Whichever you pick, get the offer on paper and settle who pays each transfer charge. Then gather the latest tax bill, parcel number, permit records and any payoff statement so the title company can set the closing date.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Mount Prospect
sections.html:
A sale here runs in a handful of steps, and most delays come from paperwork that waited until the last week.

  1. Sign the contract and settle who pays each transfer charge: state, county and village.
  2. Deliver the Illinois disclosure report before the contract is signed, with repair invoices for any past basement water.
  3. Contact Finance about the village transfer stamp. Ask whether it is bought online or in person by appointment, and what the current rate is.
  4. Bring your latest Cook County tax bill and parcel number to the title company so it can split the year's tax between buyer and seller.
  5. Pay off any loan, confirm the water, sewer and refuse account is settled with the village, and record the deed with the county.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting schedule, which is why the closing date is often the part you control. If the deed only removes a person, such as after a divorce, ask Finance about the affidavit of no consideration instead of the standard stamp.

Keep copies of everything you sign. If a question comes up later about permits, taxes or the water account, those papers are your answer, and a buyer's attorney will ask for several of them anyway.

sections.h2: What to bring to Finance and the title company
sections.html:
Before you call Finance, have the property address and parcel number ready, along with the name on the deed and the name of the buyer. If the transfer has no price, say so up front, because that points to the affidavit of no consideration. If the deed is a standard sale, ask whether the village stamp can be bought online or whether you need to book an in-person appointment, and how far ahead of closing to do it.

The title company will want the latest tax bill, the payoff figure for any loan, and a list of any open code notices or permits. Handing these over together saves a round of calls and keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: Does Mount Prospect have its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Finance sells the village's transfer stamps, online or in person by appointment. Ask it for the current rate and who pays, because the village sets this apart from the state and county charges.

faqs.q: How much is the Cook County transfer fee?
faqs.a: Cook County charges twenty-five cents per $500 and the state charges fifty cents per $500, with the seller liable for each.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Mount Prospect house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Central areas are in District 57, north and east areas in River Trails District 26, south and west areas in District 59, and small northern pockets in Districts 21, 25 and 23. Township High School District 214 covers the whole village.

faqs.q: What if I need to remove someone from a Mount Prospect deed?
faqs.a: Finance has an affidavit declaring no consideration for exempt transfers like taking a person off a deed. Ask Finance whether your situation qualifies.

faqs.q: When are Cook County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Tax year 2025 bills were due April 1, 2026 and October 1, 2026. Other years use different dates, so check your own bill.
